review.tagline: Single Go binary memory for coding agents on SQLite FTS5 with MCP
review.summary: Engram is one Go binary that stores agent memory in a local SQLite database with FTS5 full-text search and exposes it over MCP stdio, a CLI, a local HTTP API and an interactive TUI. The engram setup command configures 14 agents including Claude Code, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Codex, Cursor and Windsurf; memory is project-aware, can sync through Git as compressed chunks, and optionally replicates to Engram Cloud.
review.audience: Developers wanting dependency-free local memory across coding agents
strengths: No Node.js, Python or Docker; one binary and one SQLite file
engram setup targets 14 agents plus any MCP-compatible client
Git Sync shares memory across machines without a server
engram doctor and binary self-tests for diagnostics; MIT license
weaknesses: Full-text search only; no vector or semantic retrieval mentioned
Engram Cloud replication is optional and separate from the local store
Project detection can halt with project_transition_conflict after git init
Install docs for Windows and Linux live in docs/, not the README
